input.description: Read store.ts and search for task usages

input.reason: I read src/tasks.ts in full and searched src/ for any TaskStore implementation, callers, or guards. createFixTask builds the task as `{ id, state: "running", feedback: null }` (line 14) and persists it with `store.insert(task)` (line 15). It writes the feedback in a separate `store.update(id, { feedback })` call (line 16), with no transaction or lock around the two writes. poll (lines 21-24) runs every task that `store.runnable()` returns and never checks feedback. So a task that is visible between the two writes can be run with null feedback. Nothing ever assigns `feedback` to the local `task` object, so `emit({ ...task })` (line 17) and the returned task both carry `feedback: null`. src/store.ts only implements repo storage, not TaskStore, and I found no guard that closes the window.
input.summary: createFixTask race: task running before feedback written, stale emit

findings.text: `createFixTask` inserts the task as `running` with `feedback: null` and writes the feedback in a second statement. `poll` can pick the task up between the two writes and run it without feedback, and `emit` sends `{ ...task }` with the stale `null` feedback.
findings.reason: Claim 1 (inserted as running with null feedback): line 14 builds `{ id, state: "running", feedback: null }` and line 15 inserts it. Claim 2 (feedback written in a second statement): line 16 `await store.update(id, { feedback })` is a separate awaited call with no transaction or lock around the two writes. Claim 3 (poll can pick it up and run it without feedback): poll (lines 21-24) runs every task from `store.runnable()` and never checks `feedback`. Between the awaits at lines 15 and 16 the stored task is `running` with null feedback, so a concurrent poll can run it. The repo has no TaskStore implementation that filters such tasks out, which is why the finding says 'can'. Claim 4 (stale emit): nothing assigns `feedback` to the local `task` object after line 14, so `emit({ ...task })` at line 17 sends `feedback: null`, and the task returned at line 18 also has null feedback.

input.severity_reason: Every createFixTask call emits and returns a task with null feedback, no matter the timing, so consumers of the event always get wrong data on the main path. On top of that, the non-atomic insert-then-update lets a concurrent poll run a fix task with no feedback.
